question.problem:
A dried apricot producer knows that $70%$ of apricots weigh more than $40$ g. If the factory randomly samples $350$ apricots, find a normal approximation for the probability that fewer than $224$ apricots weigh more than $40$ g. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=350,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.7.$

Now, since

$$
np=350(0.7)=245>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=350(1-0.7)=105>5,
$$

and $n=350$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.7,\frac{0.7(1-0.7)}{350}) \\  & ∼N(0.7,0.0006).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If fewer than $224$ apricots in the sample weigh more than $40$ g, then 

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}<\frac{224}{350}=0.64.
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.64).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.64) & =P(Z<\frac{0.64-0.7}{\sqrt{0.0006}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-2.45) \\  & =Φ(-2.45).\end{aligned}
$$
